newsitem.title: UK: BA says union agrees deal to slim cargo unit.
newsitem.headline: BA says union agrees deal to slim cargo unit.

text.p: British Airways Plc on Friday said unions representing staff at its cargo division had endorsed a plan to freeze wages and cut jobs at the unit after the restructuring was approved by workers in a ballot last month.
Three-quarters of the staff at British Airways World Cargo voted in favour of the measures, which include a two-year pay freeze and the loss of 400 jobs.

British Airways said that in the light of this endorsement it was "bizarre and regrettable" for the Transport and General Workers Union (TGWU) to oppose the proposed sale of its longhaul catering division.
BA faces strike action at the start of its busy summer season over Monday's call for a strike ballot of 9,000 ground staff members over plans to close the catering business.

A BA spokesman said that the same drive for greater business efficiency underpinned both plans and that it was therefore confusing to see why unions could agree changes in one, but threaten strike action at the other.
